h1: The 6 Best Printers for Documents of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Printers for Documents: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six printers for text and document printing in 2026, covering laser and inkjet, duplex, document feeders and ink costs.
summary: The Brother DCP-L2640DW monochrome laser is our top pick for text-heavy documents. The Canon imageCLASS MF753Cdw II is the pick for color at volume with a document feeder. The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e is the pick for mixed documents at a lower upfront cost.
intro: Most people buy a printer for the color and photo features, then spend its life printing black text. For documents, the print engine and duplex capability matter more than a photo-quality color gamut, and picking the wrong type means paying for ink you do not need.
We reviewed six printers across laser and inkjet on listed engine type, duplex printing, document feeder and ink or toner design. Cheaper inkjets that suit only light use are noted as such.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A compact monochrome laser built for sharp, durable text.
products.description:
The DCP-L2640DW is a monochrome laser with duplex printing, wireless and mobile printing, and toner that fuses to paper so text does not feather. Its output is described as archivally stable.

It tops the list because it does one job, text on paper, in the way laser is best at. The tradeoff is that it prints in black only, so it cannot handle color charts.

It suits home offices and students printing contracts, reports and forms. It sits in the $200-500 range.
products.idealFor: Text-heavy documents that need to stay sharp and legible for years.

products.name: Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II Wireless Duplex Laser Printer
products.verdict: A 35 ppm color laser with an auto document feeder and a 3-year warranty.
products.description:
The MF753Cdw II is a color laser with an auto document feeder, 35 ppm print speed, duplex printing and a 3-year limited warranty.

It ranks second because it handles both text and color at a speed none of the other picks match, but it costs more and takes more space than the monochrome Brother.

It suits a small office or busy household. The document feeder makes scanning and copying multi-page files practical.
products.idealFor: A household or small office needing sharp text plus color documents at real volume.
products.skipIf: You print only a few pages a week.

products.name: Brother HL-L3220CDW Wireless Color Laser Printer
products.verdict: A 19 ppm color laser with a 250-sheet tray and duplex.
products.description:
The HL-L3220CDW is a color laser with 19 ppm speed, a 250-sheet paper tray, duplex printing and mobile device compatibility.

It ranks third because it is slower than the Canon at 35 ppm and lacks a listed document feeder, but it brings color laser quality to the same $200-500 range with a lower profile.

It suits regular document output with occasional color. It is a printer only, so scanning needs another device.
products.idealFor: Regular document output that wants laser quality without the highest-end price.
products.skipIf: You need scanning or a feeder.

products.name: Brother INKvestment MCF-J5010DW Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One
products.verdict: An inkjet with high-capacity INKvestment cartridges and automatic 2-sided copy and scan.
products.description:
The MCF-J5010DW pairs INKvestment ink tanks that need replacing less often with two-sided copying and scanning, a 2.7-inch touchscreen and wireless color inkjet printing.

It ranks fourth because it offers inkjet color flexibility with less frequent refills, yet it costs as much as the lasers above. It is the choice if you want an all-in-one with two-sided scanning.

It suits higher-volume home offices that want copy and scan tools.
products.idealFor: Higher-volume document printing that still wants inkjet color flexibility.
products.skipIf: You want lowest cost per text page.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A $50-100 inkjet with an auto document feeder and duplex.
products.description:
The OfficeJet Pro 8125e comes with a feeder for stacks of pages, two-sided printing, AI-enabled setup and a 3-month Instant Ink trial, all in a color inkjet body.

It ranks fifth because it undercuts the lasers on price while keeping a feeder, but inkjet ink costs show up over time. The Instant Ink trial only softens that for three months.

It suits mixed text and color at lower volume. Check the ink subscription terms before enrolling.
products.idealFor: Mixed text and color document printing without a laser's upfront cost.
products.skipIf: You print heavy volumes of text.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: A basic wireless all-in-one with a document feeder and built-in fax.
products.description:
The PIXMA TR4720 is a wireless all-in-one with an auto document feeder, built-in fax, mobile printing support and standard cartridges.

It ranks last because it lacks a listed duplex mode, unlike the others, and uses standard cartridges that run out sooner. It is the only pick with a fax.

It suits light scanning and fax needs on a budget. Heavy printers will outgrow it.
products.idealFor: Budget document scanning and printing with occasional multi-page needs.

whatMatters.detail: Laser printers fuse toner to paper, giving sharp text that does not smear. Inkjets cost less upfront but ink is pricier over time. For mostly text, check that the listing says laser.
Duplex means automatic two-sided printing, which halves paper use. Without it you flip pages by hand. Look for duplex or 2-sided in the specs.
An auto document feeder scans or copies multi-page files without placing each sheet. It matters for contracts. Check the listing for a feeder.
Pages per minute shows how fast a long document finishes. The picks range from 19 to 35 ppm where listed. Check the ppm number.
Consumables are the real long-term cost. High-capacity cartridges mean fewer replacements. Check how the listing describes cartridge capacity or subscriptions.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Duplex printing, a wireless connection and toner that does not fade or smear.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Brother DCP-L2640DW lists duplex, wireless and mobile printing, plus smear-free toner.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print many pages or need color and a feeder. The Canon MF753Cdw II offers 35 ppm and a 3-year warranty.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print little. The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e and Canon PIXMA TR4720 sit in the $50-100 range.

faq.a: Usually, yes. Toner fuses to the page for sharp, non-feathering text, as on the Brother DCP-L2640DW.
Buying on color features when you print mostly text, and then paying for ink you do not need.

faq.q: Is the Canon MF753Cdw II worth it over the Brother HL-L3220CDW?
faq.a: If you need a document feeder and 35 ppm speed, yes. The Brother is slower at 19 ppm.

faq.q: How do I set up wireless printing?
faq.a: Connect the printer to your Wi-Fi from its control panel or app, then add it from your device. Follow the maker's steps.

faq.q: How do I cut ink costs?
faq.a: Choose high-capacity cartridges such as Brother INKvestment, or a laser printer, which uses toner.

faq.q: Do I need a printer with a feeder?
faq.a: Only if you scan or copy multi-page documents. The Canon, HP and PIXMA picks list one.

finalTake: For most document printing, the Brother DCP-L2640DW is the best choice because it does text sharply and durably. Pick the Canon MF753Cdw II if you want color at volume with a feeder. Light users can save with the HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e.
